papers.title: Mobility-Aware Resource Allocation for mmWave IAB Networks: A Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Approach
papers.abstract: MmWaves have been envisioned as a promising direction to provide Gbps wireless access. However, they are susceptible to high path losses and blockages, which directional antennas can only partially mitigate. That makes mmWave networks coverage-limited, thus requiring dense deployments. Integrated access and backhaul (IAB) architectures have emerged as a cost-effective solution for network densification. Resource allocation in mmWave IAB networks must face big challenges to cope with heavy temporal dynamics, such as intermittent links caused by user mobility and blockages from moving obstacles. This makes it extremely difficult to find optimal and adaptive solutions. In this article, exploiting the distributed structure of the problem, we propose a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework to optimize user throughput via flow routing and link scheduling in mmWave IAB networks characterized by user mobility and link outages generated by moving obstacles. The proposed approach implicitly captures the environment dynamics, coordinates the interference, and manages the buffer levels of IAB relay nodes. We design different MARL components, considering full-duplex and half-duplex IAB-nodes. In addition, we provide a communication and coordination scheme for RL agents in an online training framework, addressing the feasibility issues of practical systems. Numerical results show the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

papers.title: Efficient Resource Allocation for On-Demand Mobile-Edge Cloud Computing
papers.abstract: Mobile-edge cloud computing is a new paradigm to provide cloud computing capabilities at the edge of pervasive radio access networks in close proximity to mobile users. Aiming at provisioning flexible on-demand mobile-edge cloud service, in this paper we propose a comprehensive framework consisting of a resource-efficient computation offloading mechanism for users and a joint communication and computation (JCC) resource allocation mechanism for network operator. Specifically, we first study the resource-efficient computation offloading problem for a user, in order to reduce user's resource occupation by determining its optimal communication and computation resource profile with minimum resource occupation and meanwhile satisfying the QoS constraint. We then tackle the critical problem of user admission control for JCC resource allocation, in order to properly select the set of users for resource demand satisfaction. We show the admission control problem is NP-hard, and hence develop an efficient approximation solution of a low complexity by carefully designing the user ranking criteria and rigourously derive its performance guarantee. To prevent the manipulation that some users may untruthfully report their valuations in acquiring mobile-edge cloud service, we further resort to the powerful tool of critical value approach to design truthful pricing scheme for JCC resource allocation. Extensive performance evaluation demonstrates that the proposed schemes can achieve superior performance for on-demand mobile-edge cloud computing.

papers.title: A Survey of Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning with Communication
papers.abstract: Communication is an effective mechanism for coordinating the behaviors of multiple agents, broadening their views of the environment, and to support their collaborations. In the field of multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL), agents can improve the overall learning performance and achieve their objectives by communication. Agents can communicate various types of messages, either to all agents or to specific agent groups, or conditioned on specific constraints. With the growing body of research work in MADRL with communication (Comm-MADRL), there is a lack of a systematic and structural approach to distinguish and classify existing Comm-MADRL approaches. In this paper, we survey recent works in the Comm-MADRL field and consider various aspects of communication that can play a role in designing and developing multi-agent reinforcement learning systems. With these aspects in mind, we propose 9 dimensions along which Comm-MADRL approaches can be analyzed, developed, and compared. By projecting existing works into the multi-dimensional space, we discover interesting trends. We also propose some novel directions for designing future Comm-MADRL systems through exploring possible combinations of the dimensions.

summary: The literature on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing reveals two primary themes: optimizing resource allocation in cloud-based systems and addressing challenges in mobile-edge cloud computing. Studies demonstrate the potential of MARL frameworks to enhance user throughput and coordination in dynamic environments, yet they often lack empirical validation and comprehensive communication strategies. Additionally, the need for adaptive resource allocation mechanisms that respond to user behavior and network fluctuations is emphasized, highlighting significant gaps in current methodologies.
scholarly_positioning: While existing research on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for resource allocation in cloud computing has demonstrated promising frameworks for optimizing performance in dynamic environments, significant limitations persist. Notably, the lack of empirical evaluations and real-world implementations undermines the practical applicability of these frameworks. Furthermore, the current literature fails to adequately address the complexities of communication strategies among agents, which are crucial for enhancing coordination and learning efficiency. This proposed research aims to bridge these gaps by developing a robust MARL framework that incorporates adaptive resource allocation mechanisms responsive to user behavior and network fluctuations, thereby contributing to the ongoing discourse on effective resource management in cloud computing.

research_scope: This empirical study will investigate the application of a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing environments, specifically targeting cloud-based deep learning systems. The evaluation period will span six months, during which the MARL framework will be tested against a baseline resource allocation strategy in a simulated environment that mimics real-world user behavior and network fluctuations. Primary outcomes will include improvements in resource utilization efficiency and user throughput, while secondary outcomes will assess the effectiveness of communication strategies among agents in enhancing coordination and learning efficiency. The study aims to provide empirical validation of MARL frameworks and explore adaptive mechanisms that respond to dynamic user demands and network conditions.
concept_definition: 1. Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL): A framework where multiple agents learn to make decisions by interacting with an environment and each other to optimize resource allocation. 2. Dynamic Resource Allocation: The process of distributing computing resources in real-time based on varying user demands and network conditions. 3. Cloud Computing: A model that enables on-demand access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources (e.g., servers, storage) over the internet. 4. Deep Learning Systems: Advanced computational models that use neural networks with many layers to analyze data and make predictions. 5. Empirical Evaluation: A research methodology involving systematic observation and experimentation to assess the effectiveness of the MARL framework compared to baseline strategies. 6. Communication Strategies: Techniques employed by agents to share information and coordinate actions, which may include direct messaging, broadcasting, or shared memory. 7. Coordination: The ability of agents to work together effectively to achieve a common goal, influenced by their communication strategies. 8. Learning Efficiency: The rate at which agents improve their decision-making capabilities based on experiences. 9. User Throughput: The rate at which users can successfully complete tasks in the cloud environment, reflecting the effectiveness of resource allocation. 10. Resource Utilization Efficiency: A measure of how effectively the available resources are used to meet user demands, aiming to minimize waste and maximize performance.
technical_feasibility: The proposed study is technically feasible as it primarily involves simulation in a controlled environment, which does not require human participants or ethics approval. However, it will require access to GPU resources for running the MARL framework and potentially open-source models for effective implementation. Since the study focuses on communication strategies among agents, it may benefit from labeled datasets to evaluate the effectiveness of these strategies. If internal representations are to be analyzed, access to open-source models or hidden-state information may be necessary. A feasible adjustment would be to ensure access to appropriate simulation tools and datasets while confirming GPU resource availability.
gap: Prior studies have demonstrated the effectiveness of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) frameworks in optimizing resource allocation in cloud-based deep learning systems; however, they treat communication strategies among agents as secondary, leaving unclear whether these strategies significantly affect coordination and learning efficiency in dynamic environments. This matters practically because effective communication can enhance agent collaboration, leading to improved resource utilization. Therefore, this study investigates the impact of various communication strategies within a MARL framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing.
question: How do different communication strategies within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework impact resource utilization efficiency and user throughput in dynamic resource allocation for cloud-based deep learning systems compared to a baseline resource allocation strategy?
theoretical_mechanism: In this study, the independent variable is the communication strategy employed by agents within the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework. The mediator is the coordination among agents, which is influenced by the effectiveness of the communication strategies. The dependent variables are resource utilization efficiency and user throughput in dynamic resource allocation scenarios. The theoretical framework is based on the principles of MARL, where agents learn to optimize resource allocation through interaction. The causal chain suggests that improved communication strategies enhance coordination, leading to better resource allocation outcomes. System-level outcomes include resource utilization efficiency, while user-level outcomes focus on user throughput. Assumptions requiring empirical validation include the effectiveness of communication strategies in enhancing coordination and the direct impact of coordination on resource allocation performance.
hypothesis: Implementing advanced communication strategies within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning framework will significantly improve resource utilization efficiency compared to a baseline resource allocation strategy, with enhanced coordination among agents mediating this effect.

methodology: This study will employ a simulation-based approach to evaluate the effectiveness of various communication strategies within a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing. The simulation environment will mimic real-world user behavior and network fluctuations, allowing for the testing of the MARL framework against a baseline resource allocation strategy. Key operationalized variables include communication strategy (independent variable), coordination (mediator), and resource utilization efficiency and user throughput (dependent variables). Evaluation metrics will consist of resource usage statistics and user task completion rates, collected at the end of the study period. To control for confounding variables such as user demand variability and network conditions, the simulation will incorporate randomized user profiles and dynamic network scenarios. The study aims for reproducibility by documenting the simulation setup and parameters, ensuring that results can be independently verified and generalized to similar cloud computing contexts.

proposal: This research proposal aims to investigate the application of Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) for dynamic resource allocation in cloud computing, specifically targeting cloud-based deep learning systems. Key concepts such as MARL, dynamic resource allocation, and communication strategies among agents will be operationally defined to ensure clarity. The study is technically feasible, relying on simulation environments that mimic real-world user behavior and network fluctuations, with access to GPU resources and open-source models assumed. Existing literature reveals promising yet under-validated MARL frameworks, highlighting a significant gap regarding the impact of communication strategies on agent coordination and learning efficiency, which has not been sufficiently explored. Thus, the research question focuses on how different communication strategies within a MARL framework affect resource utilization efficiency and user throughput compared to a clearly defined baseline resource allocation strategy. The theoretical mechanism posits that improved communication strategies enhance coordination (mediator), leading to better resource allocation outcomes (system-level) and increased user throughput (user-level). The falsifiable hypothesis states that implementing advanced communication strategies will significantly improve resource utilization efficiency compared to the baseline strategy, mediated by enhanced coordination. Constructs will be operationalized using agent interaction logs for communication strategy (IV), coordination efficiency metrics (mediator), and resource usage statistics and user task completion rates (DVs), all collected in a controlled simulation environment. The methodology will employ a simulation-based approach with randomized user profiles and dynamic network scenarios to control for confounding variables, ensuring robustness. Expected contributions include theoretical advancements in understanding agent communication dynamics, technical development of a novel MARL framework, empirical evidence from a six-month evaluation, and practical guidelines for cloud computing practitioners. Key limitations include potential confounding factors such as user demand variability and the inability to generalize findings beyond the tested scenarios, alongside risks related to communication strategy effectiveness and data sparsity, which will be mitigated through diverse user profiles and preliminary testing of communication strategies.
